title: Interval List Intersections
summary: Given two lists of closed intervals, where each interval is represented as [start, end] and both lists are sorted and pairwise disjoint, find the intersection of these intervals by identifying the overlapping segments between corresponding intervals from both lists.
statement: Given two lists of closed intervals, where each interval is represented as [start, end] and both lists are sorted and pairwise disjoint, find the intersection of these intervals by identifying the overlapping segments between corresponding intervals from both lists.
constraints: Each list contains sorted, pairwise-disjoint closed intervals.
Return all nonempty intersections in increasing order.
hints: Two current intervals intersect from max starts to min ends when that range is nonempty.
Append [max(lefts),min(rights)] when start<=end, then move the earlier end pointer.
The earlier-ending interval cannot intersect any later interval in the other list after this comparison.
editorial: The earlier-ending interval cannot intersect any later interval in the other list after this comparison.

tests.explanation: The two-pointer scan produces six closed intersections, including touching endpoints.
An empty second list has no intersections.
